children: Extreme weather exacerbated by the ongoing El Niño episode could further undermine commodity markets, worsening the impact of high fertilizer prices and disrupting other climate-sensitive sectors like transportation, the IMF warns. Past episodes have shown that El Niño typically drives up food and commodity prices while weighing on activity, especially in economies where food is a major share of the consumer basket. Such risks are particularly acute for energy importers, especially emerging and developing economies with limited fiscal space and external buffers. Persistently higher commodity prices could widen current account deficits and intensify exchange-rate pressures. Higher inflation could meanwhile require tighter monetary policy, further dragging growth.(fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
